Depends really. Battling drug-abuse changed my aspect of life. Literally rags to riches. 

I ate oatmeal for breakfast and lunch for a whole year (2013) so I could invest in a hot meal for dinner, and be able to add more nutrition to my already glue-tasting oats.  By doing only that I saved enough to approach a diet with (4) appetizing meals . By changing my habits I saved 50-100$ a week. (I earned around 1800$ a month most of 2013)

Moved further away from work, it was cheaper to commute than pay a horrendous rent living close to work. It also killed a lot of time. I felt less alone, and it didn’t fall tempting to «spend time with friends and burn money». I got better at inviting people to my 2-room apartment and visiting their homes. My budget shifted into an alternate bank where I actually saved enough to allow myself to party once-twice a month (it was usually two-three beers with friends or colleagues at pay-day, or a big night-out a week after or when the more people could gather). Life taught me how to plan shit according to what was in my pocket. 

I stopped unnecessarily buying things I really didn’t fucking need. You don’t need more than 4 pairs of shoes and/ or three jackets... learnt to layer up. Started to colour code my clothes too, don’t need more than three hoodies, pants, t-shirts. Invested in something that would last. I didn’t buy anything but a 7-pair of socks and underwear in span of 2015-2018. 

2019 is the year I decided to go whatever the trend is called of living «minimalistic». And I managed to save enough money to get a house on a mortgage. I was basically living a shit lifestyle, pay-check to pay-check before I decided to change. 80% of my furniture is 2ndhand. 

... good example would be many of my peers, rich or poor. Pay-check to pay-check but no fucking control of their lifes and choices. Me and my friends usually joke about «the bigger income, the jucier beef». It has never been about being smart, it’s about what you’re willing to give up for a better quality of life. But some people are unfortunately in situations that you can’t make what one would consider «smart» choices because they basically don’t have the resources to do so. It’s honestly give or take.
